_: Policy for the claim lint. The lint reads this; docs/design/CONTRACTS.md points at it. It is inside the same ratchet as everything else, because the file the checks trust must not be the file nobody watches.

guarantee_terms_deliberately_absent.records?: matches product-status assertions ('records the outcome') far more often than invariants
guarantee_terms_deliberately_absent.ships?: same, and it matches 'relationships' and 'flagship' as substrings

guarantee_terms_note: The first term is `every`/`all` restricted to quantification over BEHAVIOUR: the quantifier must sit within a short span of a verb that does something to a request, a charge or a principal. Unrestricted, it captured statements of fact about configuration ('every table is provisioned in PAY_PER_REQUEST mode'), which are not promises and have no honest anchor kind. See amendment 10 of the change contract. Each term carries its own word boundaries: a single wrapper around the whole alternation silently broke every prefix term, because no boundary can follow the 'c' of 'enforc' when the text says 'enforces'.
third_party_subjects_note: Competing products and external actors whose behaviour a sentence may describe. NOT services this gateway is built on — DynamoDB, Bedrock, Cognito, STS and CloudFront were on this list once, and 'Every route enforces … with atomic DynamoDB reservations' escaped the protected-subject floor because of it. Naming infrastructure is what a sentence about our own mechanism looks like. Amendments 11 and 12 of the change contract have the reasoning and the residue.
document_scope_note: A sentence whose subject is the document rather than the system may take `descriptive:` even though it names the project — 'This document describes … the invariants Stratoclave relies on' asserts nothing about behaviour. Narrow on purpose: the sentence has to BEGIN this way, which is not a form anyone reaches for by accident. Amendment 13.
protected_subjects_note: Word-bounded on purpose: without boundaries `Pool` matched inside `UserPoolClient` and `Bearer` inside `CallWithBearerToken`, so a CDK warning and an IAM limitation were treated as money guarantees. `hold` was dropped entirely — as a bare word it is a verb at least as often as a noun ('it does not hold for a role'), and the money meaning is already carried by `reservation`, `reserve` and `pool`. Amendment 14.

floor_exemptions_note: Per-id, with a reason each, because the alternative was widening the floor for everyone. An enumerated list is reviewable and a widened rule is not: `test_claim_judgement_worklist.py` prints these, so the population stays visible. Two of them — the operator's duty about directly-assumable role patterns — are a real gap and are on the open items.
